title: Academic register
summary: Dense wording and abstract nouns. Harder to hold because the words carry less picture.

sentences.text: The correlation was statistically significant but substantively trivial.
These findings are consistent with the hypothesis but do not confirm it.
The methodology section omits any account of how participants were selected.
Subsequent replication attempts yielded considerably weaker effects.
The distinction between correlation and causation is routinely ignored in reporting.
Peer review is intended to catch confusion rather than deliberate fraud.
The sample was drawn exclusively from undergraduate volunteers.
Her interpretation depends on an assumption the data cannot test.
The literature offers no consensus on how the term should be defined.
Quantitative methods dominate the field for largely historical reasons.
The variables were controlled for age, income and prior education.
Publication bias makes the published literature unrepresentative of the research conducted.
The theoretical framework was borrowed almost unchanged from an adjacent discipline.
Longitudinal data would resolve the ambiguity, but none exists.
The authors acknowledge that their sample size limits any generalisation.
Empirical support for the model remains largely indirect.
The paper conflates two distinct phenomena throughout its argument.
Qualitative interviews revealed motivations the survey had entirely missed.
The proposed mechanism is plausible but has never been directly observed.
Reviewers raised concerns about the reliability of the coding procedure.
